A prime has exactly two positive divisors, 1 and itself. An integer greater than 1 that is not prime is composite.
The fundamental theorem of arithmetic says this factorization exists and is unique apart from the order of the factors.

items.text: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite; its prime factorization is the empty product.
For negative integers, factor the absolute value and record a separate factor -1.
Uniqueness concerns prime factors with multiplicity, not arbitrary factorizations into composite numbers.

A failed divisibility test by a few small primes does not by itself prove primality.
Distinct prime factors and prime factors counted with multiplicity are different counts.
